title: UX-driven accessibility gap analysis and VPAT checklist for data components
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Run a UX-led gap analysis across dense data components (tables, charts, data grids, action rows) to prepare a VPAT-ready compliance checklist and prioritized remediation list. This ticket consolidates findings from the component-level contrast and keyboard/role audits and produces a clear handoff pack for engineering to implement fixes and for QA to validate.

Why now: We have an enterprise customer asking for VPAT artifacts tied to our 2026.03 release. Recent dashboard work surfaced inconsistent focus rings, multiple instances of insufficient chart legend contrast at small sizes, and ambiguous ARIA roles on interactive cell controls. This task is scoped to identify concrete fixes that are feasible within the release and to produce acceptance criteria and test cases.

Scope: tokens (contrast ramp and focus token mapping), button-like cells, sortable/interactive table headers, drilldown chart tooltips & legends, and dense keyboard navigation patterns. Not in scope: full platform VPAT sign-off or legal review (that will be handled by Compliance after we deliver the checklist).
acceptance_criteria: Deliver a prioritized remediation backlog with severity and estimated points for each item
Produce a VPAT-aligned checklist document mapping WCAG criteria to affected components
Provide Figma token updates (contrast and focus) and example component variants demonstrating fixes
Engineering has a runnable test plan with deterministic steps for keyboard nav and contrast checks
QA has signed off on verification steps for at least 3 high-impact components (table row focus, chart legend contrast, compact action buttons)
design_notes: I created a focus heatmap prototype in Figma that overlays current focus-visible states across table and chart variants. Key observations: (1) Dense rows use the same focus token as buttons which creates a visual conflict when rows contain multiple interactive elements; (2) Small-legend text in charts at 10px frequently fails contrast at dark mode; (3) Sort icons are not announced consistently because aria-sort is missing on some header cells. Proposed approach: introduce a dedicated 'dense-row-focus' token with 3px stroke and 6% elevated background, update chart legend token to increase contrast to meet 4.5:1 at minimum for small text, and create a header role audit checklist to standardize aria-sort/aria-labels.
dev_notes: Engineers: expect 2 PRs. PR A updates CSS tokens and theme maps (affects tokens package + design tokens migration). PR B updates table and chart components to use new tokens and applies aria attributes for header cells and interactive cell buttons. Perf note: adding focus outlines on dense lists may add repaints—use outline-offset and avoid box-shadow where possible. Workaround for charts: update text color token and re-render legend layer only when theme changes. See github links in 'links'.
test_plan: Keyboard nav: ensure Tab/Shift-Tab cycles through row-level controls, Enter/Space activates row-level primary action, Arrow keys move within cell focusable controls as per component spec
Screen reader: NVDA/VoiceOver test script for table headers, ensure aria-sort announces state and aria-describedby is used for combined labels
Contrast tests: automated color-contrast screenshot diff for legend text at small sizes (10px/12px) across themes
Regression: run visual diffs for table row hover/focus across density settings and token variants
decisions: Adopt a dedicated dense-row-focus token instead of reusing button focus to reduce visual ambiguity
Raise minimum legend contrast for small text to 4.5:1 instead of 3:1 for improved legibility in data dense contexts
Standardize header accessibility pattern: table headers use role=columnheader with explicit aria-sort and aria-label where the visible label differs from semantic label
comments: 2026-02-22 Maya C: Initial heatmap uploaded to Figma; flagged 12 instances of insufficient contrast in chart legends.
2026-02-25 Omar P (Eng): Reviewed token changes; requested perf guidance for focus outline approach. Added dev_notes recommendation.

2026-03-04 Priya S (PM): Confirmed we can include 3 critical fixes in 2026.03 release; lower priority items moved to backlog.

Engineer implements aria updates and table focus behavior (owner: Omar)
QA runs scripted tests and records passes/failures in the QA checklist doc
Hand off VPAT checklist to Compliance for formal review
